mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2.5% signals robust household demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in periods where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and inflation, which in turn raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when UNRATE < 4.5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when INDPRO falls > 1.5% over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a disinflationary tightening cycle, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.5% over three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 for three consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when PAYEMS rises > 100,000 for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 500,000 units for three consecutive months signals a housing market slowdown that reduces household wealth and spending, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when HOUST < 500,000 for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below 1% signals weak household demand growth, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when GDPC1 YoY growth < 1% (t-test p > 0.05).
